root_cause.text: The XFS attr leaf freemap update code in `xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work` leaves behind zero-length freemap entries with a nonzero base, which can combine with a separate bug in the freemap update logic during entry expansion to create overlapping freemap entries, leading to data corruption when subsequent allocations overwrite the entries array.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message state that "This code can leave behind a zero-length freemap entry with a nonzero base" and that "there's another bug in the freemap update code in _leaf_add, which is that it fails to update a freemap entry that begins midway through the xattr entry that was just appended to the array. That can result in the freemap containing two entries with the same base but different sizes... A subsequent _leaf_add can then allocate xattr namevalue entries on top of the entries array, leading to data loss." The patch fixes the first part by zeroing the base of zero-size entries to prevent confusion.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential corruption of free space maps by resetting base of zero-length entries and marking holes in xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work.
intent_record.what: Added a check after the freemap update loop in xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work that resets the base of zero-length freemap entries to 0 and sets ichdr->holes = 1 to avoid overlapping freemaps.
intent_record.how: Prevents zero-length freemap entries with nonzero base from causing confusion in the _remove function, which could lead to overlapping free space maps; also ensures that if no freemap entries remain, the next add will compact and regenerate the freemaps.
